BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. 380	// Deliberately NOT keyed on the push remote. The predecessor compared the push
381	// destination's owner, which conflates "is this setting mine" with "where is this
382	// particular push going": pushing to any differently-owned remote (a backup, a
383	// colleague's fork) disabled the user's own checkpoint_remote and sent the
384	// checkpoints to that remote instead. It also has no single answer for a remote
385	// carrying several push URLs with different owners, where one boolean has to
386	// cover the whole set — still the case on the git-branch backend, which fans out
387	// to every push URL.
388	//
389	// An origin whose owner cannot be determined (no origin remote, or a non-forge
390	// URL such as a bare local path) counts as inherited: for a committed setting we
391	// cannot confirm ownership, and falling back preserves the previous behavior for
392	// those repos. settings.local.json is the escape hatch when the checkpoint repo
393	// is genuinely ours but owned by a different account or org than origin.
394	func checkpointRemoteIsInherited(ctx context.Context, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig, originURL, pushRemoteURL string) (bool, string) {
395		checkpointOwner := config.Owner()
396		if checkpointOwner == "" {
397			// No owner to compare (malformed repo field). Matches the predecessor,
398			// which skipped the check rather than blocking on it.
399			return false, ""
400		}
401		if settings.CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly(ctx) {
402			return false, ""
403		}
404	
405		// Origin identifies the repo we are working in. Without one, the push remote
406		// is the only identity available, and using it is what the predecessor
407		// effectively did — a repo whose only remote is e.g. "upstream" must not lose
408		// its configured checkpoint remote just because nothing is named "origin".
409		// There is no origin-vs-push-remote divergence to worry about in that case:
410		// the repo has exactly one identity.
411		identityURL, identitySource := originURL, "origin"
412		if identityURL == "" {
413			identityURL, identitySource = pushRemoteURL, "push remote"
414		}
415		if identityURL == "" {
416			return true, "no remote to establish ownership"
417		}
418	
419		info, err := ParseURL(identityURL)
420		if err != nil || info.Owner == "" {
421			return true, identitySource + " URL owner could not be determined"
422		}
423		if strings.EqualFold(info.Owner, checkpointOwner) {
424			return false, ""
425		}
426		return true, fmt.Sprintf("%s owner %q differs from checkpoint owner %q", identitySource, info.Owner, checkpointOwner)
427	}

429	// GetRemoteURLInDir returns the URL configured for the named git remote in dir.
430	func GetRemoteURLInDir(ctx context.Context, dir, remoteName string) (string, error) {
431		url, err := gitremote.GetRemoteURLInDir(ctx, dir, remoteName)
432		if err != nil {
433			return "", fmt.Errorf("get remote URL: %w", err)
434		}
435		return url, nil

438	// ParseURL parses a git remote URL (SSH SCP-style or HTTPS) into its components.
439	func ParseURL(rawURL string) (*Info, error) {
440		info, err := gitremote.ParseURL(rawURL)
441		if err != nil {
442			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse URL: %w", err)
443		}
444		return info, nil
445	}

447	// isDirectGitTransport reports whether the protocol talks to the git host
448	// directly over ssh/https (where the host is a usable HTTPS host for token
449	// auth), as opposed to a remote helper scheme like entire:// or a local
450	// file://.
451	func isDirectGitTransport(protocol string) bool {
452		return protocol == ProtocolSSH || protocol == ProtocolHTTPS
453	}

455	func deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo(info *Info, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig) (string, error) {
456		switch info.Protocol {
457		case ProtocolSSH:
458			// SCP-style (git@host:repo) doesn't support ports. When a non-default
459			// port is set (e.g., from ssh://git@host:2222/...), use the ssh:// URL form.
460			if info.Port != "" {
461				return fmt.Sprintf("ssh://git@%s/%s.git", info.HostPort(), config.Repo), nil
462			}
463			return fmt.Sprintf("git@%s:%s.git", info.Host, config.Repo), nil
464		case ProtocolHTTPS:
465			return fmt.Sprintf("https://%s/%s.git", info.HostPort(), config.Repo), nil
466		case ProtocolEntire:
467			// entire:// push-through mirrors are cluster-scoped: keep the cluster
468			// host and forge segment, swap in the checkpoint repo. Only derivable
469			// when the forge maps back to the configured provider's host, so a
470			// github checkpoint_remote never routes through another forge's mirror.
471			host, ok := providerHost(config.Provider)
472			if !ok || !strings.EqualFold(info.CanonicalHost(), host) {
473				return "", fmt.Errorf("entire:// remote forge %q does not match checkpoint provider %q", info.Forge, config.Provider)
474			}
475			return fmt.Sprintf("entire://%s/%s/%s", info.HostPort(), info.Forge, config.Repo), nil
476		default:
477			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported protocol %q in remote URL", info.Protocol)
478		}

481	// resolveProviderCheckpointURL builds the checkpoint URL for the configured
482	// provider, choosing the transport from what's already configured for that
483	// endpoint. It is the fallback used when the push/origin remote's protocol can't
484	// be mapped to a git transport (e.g. entire://, file://): the configured
485	// checkpoint_remote names a concrete provider, so checkpoints go there rather
486	// than being misrouted to the origin remote.
487	//
488	// Transport precedence:
489	//  1. ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN set -> HTTPS on the provider host (the token is
490	//     the credential).
491	//  2. An existing remote already targets the provider host -> reuse its scheme,
492	//     so checkpoints use the same auth the user already has for that endpoint.
493	//  3. Otherwise SSH on the provider host.
494	//
495	// Returns ok=false when no transport can be determined (unknown provider with no
496	// usable signal), in which case the caller falls back to the origin remote.
497	func resolveProviderCheckpointURL(ctx context.Context, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig, dir string) (string, bool) {
498		repo, err := openRepoAt(ctx, dir)
499		if err != nil {
500			repo = nil // Fall back to env/provider-only signals.
501		}
502	
503		info, ok := pickProviderTransport(repo, config)
504		if !ok {
505			return "", false
506		}
507		url, err := deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo(info, config)
508		if err != nil {
509			return "", false
510		}
511		return url, true
512	}

514	// pickProviderTransport returns the protocol/host/port to use when deriving a
515	// checkpoint URL, following the precedence documented on
516	// resolveProviderCheckpointURL.
517	func pickProviderTransport(repo *git.Repository, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig) (*Info, bool) {
518		host, hostOK := providerHost(config.Provider)
519	
520		// 1. Explicit token -> HTTPS on the provider host.
521		if hostOK && strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(CheckpointTokenEnvVar)) != "" {
522			return &Info{Protocol: ProtocolHTTPS, Host: host}, true
523		}
524	
525		// 2. An existing remote already targeting the provider host -> reuse scheme.
526		if hostOK && repo != nil {
527			if info, ok := findRemoteInfoForHost(repo, host); ok {
528				return &Info{Protocol: info.Protocol, Host: info.Host, Port: info.Port}, true
529			}
530		}
531	
532		// 3. Default to SSH on the provider host.
533		if hostOK {
534			return &Info{Protocol: ProtocolSSH, Host: host}, true
535		}

537		return nil, false
538	}

541	// empty). It routes through gitrepo, the single reftable-aware opener, so a
542	// reftable repository is opened via the git-CLI storer rather than rejected by
543	// go-git's extension check. gitrepo.OpenCurrent resolves the worktree root from
544	// the current directory (the walk-up equivalent of the previous DetectDotGit
545	// open) when no explicit root is given.
546	func openRepoAt(ctx context.Context, dir string) (*git.Repository, error) {
547		if dir == "" {
548			repo, err := gitrepo.OpenCurrent(ctx)
549			if err != nil {
550				return nil, fmt.Errorf("open git repository: %w", err)
551			}
552			return repo, nil
553		}
554		repo, err := gitrepo.OpenPath(dir)
555		if err != nil {
556			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open git repository: %w", err)
557		}
558		return repo, nil
559	}

561	// findRemoteInfoForHost returns the parsed Info of the first configured git
562	// remote (in deterministic name order) whose host matches host and whose
563	// protocol is a usable git transport (ssh/https). entire:// and other
564	// non-transport remotes are ignored.
565	func findRemoteInfoForHost(repo *git.Repository, host string) (*Info, bool) {
566		cfg, err := repo.Config()
567		if err != nil {
568			return nil, false
569		}
570		names := make([]string, 0, len(cfg.Remotes))
571		for name := range cfg.Remotes {
572			names = append(names, name)
573		}
574		sort.Strings(names)
575		for _, name := range names {
576			for _, rawURL := range cfg.Remotes[name].URLs {
577				info, err := gitremote.ParseURL(rawURL)
578				if err != nil {
579					continue
580				}
581				if strings.EqualFold(info.Host, host) && isDirectGitTransport(info.Protocol) {
582					return info, true
583				}
584			}
585		}
586		return nil, false
587	}

589	func deriveTokenOriginURL(originURL string) (string, bool) {
590		info, err := gitremote.ParseURL(originURL)
591		if err != nil {
592			return "", false
593		}
594		if info.Host == "" || info.Owner == "" || info.Repo == "" {
595			return "", false
596		}
597		// Keep the port only when the source was already HTTPS. SSH ports
598		// (e.g., :2222) don't map to HTTPS ports on the same host.
599		hostPort := info.Host
600		if info.Protocol == ProtocolHTTPS {
601			hostPort = info.HostPort()
602		}
603		return fmt.Sprintf("https://%s/%s/%s.git", hostPort, info.Owner, info.Repo), true
604	}

606	func providerHost(provider string) (string, bool) {
607		switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(provider)) {
608		case "github":
609			return "github.com", true
610		case "gitlab":
611			return "gitlab.com", true
612		default:
613			return "", false
614		}
615	}

618	func RedactURL(rawURL string) string {

620	}
